title: 2025 HMMT February Guts Problem 14
statement: A parallelogram \(P\) can be folded over a straight line so that the resulting shape is a regular pentagon with side length 1. Compute the perimeter of \(P\) .

solutions.text:
In regular pentagon \(ABCDE\) (labeled clockwise), reflect \(ABDE\) across \(AB\) to obtain \(ABD'E'\) . Then, \(CDE'D'\) is one such parallelogram \(P\) . The length of \(CD'\) is

\[CB + BD = 1 + 2\cos \angle CBD = 1 + 2\cos (\pi /5) = 1 + \frac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{5} + 3}{2}.\]

Hence, the perimeter of the desired parallelogram is \(2\left(1 + \frac{\sqrt{5} + 3}{2}\right) = \left\lfloor \frac{5 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right\rfloor\) .
